title: The Importance of Cells in Living Things

competencies.text: Describe how cells obtain nutrients and convert them into energy.

days.title: Cells — The Unit of Life
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to describe the parts of a cell, explain how cells obtain nutrients through the cell membrane, and describe how they convert those nutrients into usable energy (ATP) through cellular respiration.

🔬 What Is a Cell?

The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things. Every living organism — from bacteria to humans — is made of one or more cells.

TypeDescriptionExample
ProkaryoticNo true nucleus; DNA floats in cytoplasmBacteria
EukaryoticHas a true nucleus and membrane-bound organellesPlant, animal, fungal cells

🧩 Parts of a Cell & Their Functions

OrganelleFunctionAnalogy
Cell membraneControls what enters and exits the cellDoor / gatekeeper
CytoplasmJelly-like fluid where reactions occurFactory floor
NucleusContains DNA — the instructions for the cellManager's office
MitochondriaProduces energy (ATP) through cellular respirationPower plant
RibosomesBuilds proteinsAssembly line
Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)Transports materials inside the cellConveyor belt
Golgi apparatusPackages and ships proteinsPost office
LysosomesBreak down wasteRecycling center
VacuoleStores water, nutrients, waste (large in plants)Storage room
Chloroplast (plant only)Performs photosynthesis to make glucoseSolar panel
Cell wall (plant only)Provides structure and supportBrick wall

🍔 How Cells Obtain Nutrients

Cells get nutrients through a selectively permeable membrane — a barrier that lets some substances in and keeps others out.

ProcessDescriptionDirection
DiffusionMolecules move from high to low concentration (no energy needed)Into or out of cell
OsmosisWater moves across the membrane from high to low water concentrationInto or out of cell
Facilitated diffusionMolecules move through special channel proteinsHigh → low
Active transportMolecules move from low to high concentration using energy (ATP)Low → high
EndocytosisCell engulfs large particles or liquidsInto cell
PhagocytosisWhite blood cells engulf bacteriaInto cell

⚡ How Cells Convert Nutrients into Energy

Once nutrients enter the cell, they are broken down to release energy stored in the form of ATP (adenosine triphosphate).

C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + ~36 ATP

🔬 Three Stages of Cellular Respiration

StageWhereWhat HappensATP Produced
1. GlycolysisCytoplasmGlucose is split into two pyruvate molecules2 ATP
2. Krebs cycle (Citric Acid Cycle)Mitochondrial matrixPyruvate is broken down further; CO₂ released2 ATP
3. Electron Transport Chain (ETC)Inner mitochondrial membraneElectrons power ATP production; O₂ is final electron acceptor~32 ATP

Total: ~36 ATP per glucose molecule.

🌿 Photosynthesis vs. Respiration — A Cycle

  • Photosynthesis (plants): Uses sunlight + CO₂ + H₂O to make glucose and O₂.
  • Respiration (all cells): Uses glucose + O₂ to release energy (ATP), CO₂, and H₂O.
  • Together, they form a balanced cycle that sustains life on Earth.

🩺 Real-Life Applications

  • Medicine: Cancer cells divide uncontrollably — understanding cell division is key to treatment.
  • Nutrition: Eating balanced meals gives cells the nutrients they need to produce ATP.
  • Exercise: Muscles need more ATP — that's why you breathe faster when running.
  • Plant growth: Fertilizers provide nutrients for photosynthesis and respiration.

📌 Quick Check

  • What is the powerhouse of the cell? (Answer: mitochondria)
  • What is the energy currency of the cell? (Answer: ATP)
  • Which process moves molecules from LOW to HIGH concentration? (Answer: active transport)

days.title: Match Game — Cell Organelles
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each cell part or process to its correct function. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Controls what enters and exits the cell
Contains DNA — the instructions for the cell
Water moves across the membrane from high to low water concentration
Moves molecules from low to high concentration using ATP
The energy currency of the cell — made by mitochondria

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Cell Energy
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🏃 During a marathon, a runner's muscles need more energy than usual. What process increases inside their cells?

choices.label: B) Cellular respiration — glucose is broken down with more oxygen to produce more ATP

scenario.text: 🥔 A potato slice is placed in a very salty solution. After 30 minutes, the potato feels soft and shriveled. Why?

choices.label: A) Water left the potato cells by osmosis because the salt solution had lower water concentration
B) Salt destroyed the potato cells chemically
C) The potato absorbed the salt

scenario.text: 🦠 A white blood cell engulfs a bacterium to destroy it. What process is this?

choices.label: B) Phagocytosis — a form of endocytosis where the cell engulfs large particles

scenario.text: 🫀 A patient's cells are unable to produce enough ATP. Which organelle is most likely malfunctioning?

choices.label: B) Mitochondria — the site of ATP production

scenario.text: 🌿 A plant has plenty of sunlight, water, and CO₂. It grows well. Later, it's moved to complete darkness. Which process stops, and what happens to the plant?

choices.label: A) Photosynthesis stops (no light), but respiration continues — the plant slowly loses energy reserves
B) Both photosynthesis and respiration stop
